raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When decode reuses a finished request's KV pages while its last forward is still in flight, publishing the new destination immediately lets prefill write into pages that the old forward can still overwrite. #45328 orders the normal deferred-publication path; this PR closes the remaining device-destination paths under overlap scheduling, including staging, HiSparse, and configurations with the WAR barrier or deferred publication disabled.

PP currently disables overlap, so it keeps its existing synchronous publication behavior. Host destinations keep their existing H2D fencing.

## Modifications

- Hold inline device metadata behind an event recorded on the forward stream. Publish only after every rank agrees that its event is complete and its receiver has not failed, using a MIN reduction. This prevents partial publication across TP ranks during cancellation.
- Publish held destinations before the retraction and polling gates, and again after newly allocated requests enter the transfer queue. A retracted request cannot indefinitely delay an unrelated ready destination.
- Release unpublished failed destinations without waiting for drain acknowledgements that cannot arrive. If a peer requires a collective hold, the unpublished rank participates with zero required acknowledgements.
- For early-policy rebootstrap requests, submit prefill recomputation after the held metadata is actually sent, preserving the existing ordering and avoiding an abort before the receiver is armed.
- Initialize `chunk_staging_infos` in `CommonKVReceiver.__init__`, so staging cleanup is safe before `send_metadata`.

The existing deferred-publication and host-destination paths retain their ordering. Tests cover event readiness, agreement across ranks, retraction gating, failed receivers, acknowledgement accounting, staging cleanup, and recompute submission order. The delayed-conclusion test is defensive coverage; it does not claim that PP currently enables overlap.

## Accuracy Tests

Validation of `3f6f056ecbb977350ea9a97c9d4c7b5c74b4af50` against parent `fb9846d3e2d66811b372b28c73229e9dbbf54288`:

- Seven focused unit-test files: **100 passed, 72 subtests passed**. The new regressions fail before the fixes and pass afterward.
- All 43 disaggregation unit-test files plus the adjacent PP-outcome and retraction-backup files, each in its own process: **852 passing cases including subtests, one failure**. `TestPPConsensusStore.test_malformed_messages_are_dropped` also fails on the exact parent in this local environment; the same process hangs during ZMQ cleanup. It is unchanged by this PR.
- Real local Qwen3-8B serving on four NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, with TP=2 prefill and TP=2 decode, CUDA decode graphs, chunked prefill, decode radix caching, and KV checksums. Both inline and default deferred-publication configurations pass sequential and concurrent generation, one-token completion, 24 cancellations, 12 recovery requests, streaming, and final health checks. **All 12 sequential and 24 concurrent responses match the parent's token IDs exactly.** All 24 requests are cancelled and all 12 recovery responses match the sequential results in both final TP=2 runs.
- PP=2 prefill/decode control passes the same generation, cancellation, recovery, streaming, and health workload; its 12 sequential and 24 concurrent responses match the parent. Cancellation requests omit log probabilities to avoid a MiniLB `KeyError: meta_info` that reproduces on both parent and head.
- Heterogeneous TP staging (prefill TP=1, decode TP=2) passes generation, 24 cancellations, 12 recovery requests, streaming, and health on both parent and final source. All 12 sequential responses match; 23/24 concurrent responses match, with batch variation also observed on the parent.
- Single-GPU-per-role PD and unified-server controls also pass. These local transport tests use Mooncake TCP; they do not validate RDMA or NVLink transport.
- Focused follow-up: 16 publication/cleanup regressions pass in 12.36 seconds. A local NIXL/UCX TP=2 prefill/decode run with inline publication passes in 56.68 seconds: all 12 sequential and 24 concurrent responses match the parent, with 24 successful cancellations, 12 matching recovery responses, streaming, CUDA decode graphs, and KV checksums. UCX uses shared memory/TCP/CUDA IPC locally; RDMA is left to CI.
- Full PR-range pre-commit verification passes. Claude Code reviewed the final changes and reported no correctness blockers.
- NVIDIA [Base CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41243972189) and [Extra CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41243972132) are running on the final commit. Completed coverage includes all 20 CPU shards, basic/optimistic disaggregation, prefill-complete allocation, unified memory, HiSparse, SWA heterogeneous TP, DeepSeek heterogeneous TP, DP attention, and the previously failing canary test. A [focused H20 rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41249851467) passed the selected staging/radix, NIXL, and decode-PP tests on the final commit. The full matrix is not yet complete.

This is bounded token-parity and lifecycle validation, not a full model-accuracy evaluation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No formal performance benchmark was run. Held destinations add a nonblocking event query and a small Gloo MIN reduction while publication is pending. Queue scans return without a collective when there are no held destinations. Publication waits for the previously enqueued forward to complete and for rank agreement; no synchronous device wait is added.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests for changed behavior.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [ ] Full accuracy and speed benchmarks (not run).

@metamergebot  please take over it

Hi @libertyeagle, thanks for handing this over. The branch now carries the follow-ups found in review (the receiver creates `chunk_staging_infos` before `send_metadata` is held, and the held destination is sent only for requests still in the transfer queue, with no drain acknowledgement awaited for one that never sent it), rebased onto current main after #47063. The bot cannot take a PR out of draft, so two small asks:

1. Please mark this PR **Ready for review** so CI can run (pr-gate blocks all tests on a draft).
2. Please replace the PR description with the updated one below: it documents the follow-ups and fixes the "before it polls" sentence.

<details>
<summary>Updated PR description</summary>

## Motivation

On a PD decode server with overlap scheduling, a request that finished at step k−1 is still a row of forward k, because forward k was launched before the scheduler processed step k−1's results. `process_batch_result` frees that request's KV pages while forward k is still in flight. On the next iteration, `process_decode_queue` can preallocate those pages for a new request, and `DecodePreallocQueue._send_kv_metadata` sends them to prefill right away.

The prefill then writes the pages by RDMA, and no CUDA stream orders that write. If the RDMA lands before forward k writes the finished row's KV, forward k overwrites part of the new request's transferred KV. The new request then decodes from wrong KV, and nothing reports an error.

Two other paths already guard against this by waiting for the forward stream before they reuse pages:
- prebuilt requests (`get_new_prebuilt_batch`);
- retraction restore and write-through (#42701, #42702).

The prealloc → transfer path is the one that remains, and `wait_stream` cannot order a remote RDMA write.

Each hit corrupts one position per finished row with plain decode. With speculative decoding it corrupts one verify window, and that window can fall on a page beyond the request's committed length. Hits need a nearly full decode pool, so that a freed page is reused at once, and a prefill that is already waiting for decode memory, so that its RDMA lands within one forward.

## Modifications

When overlap scheduling is on and the destination is on the device:
- `DecodePreallocQueue._send_kv_metadata` records an event on the forward stream after allocating, instead of calling `send_metadata` right away. The event covers every forward enqueued so far. The `send_metadata` arguments are kept on the request in a new field, `DecodeRequest.pending_metadata`.
- `DecodeTransferQueue.pop_transferred` sends the held metadata once its event completes, after it polls and filters the queue, so only requests still queued send it.
- Nothing blocks. A request dropped from the transfer queue drops its held metadata with it.

The send is delayed by at most the forward in flight, about one decode step, and only while that forward is still running. Host destinations are unchanged, because the H2D copy that follows already waits for the forward.

Every transfer backend gets the fix, since they all receive destinations through `_send_kv_metadata`. That includes the staging path, whose scatter runs on its own stream.

The unit test stand-ins for `DecodeRequest` and the scheduler get the new fields (`pending_metadata=None`, `enable_overlap=False`).

## Accuracy Tests

The corruption is silent, so it was found with a KV integrity checker. The checker seals each transferred page with a checksum on prefill and verifies it when decode accepts the transfer.

The setup was PD 1P1D with overlap scheduling and a decode pool small enough to force retractions, with 4096-token prompts and 2048-token outputs at concurrency 32.

Before this change, with and without speculative decoding:
- Transferred pages failed their checksum at accept, while the page identity in the tag still matched.
- Debug output showed the forward for requests that had just finished writing into those pages after the transfer landed.

After this change: no mismatches over repeated runs (8–10 retractions and about 475 accepted transfers each), with `cpu_tensor` and `host_pool` retraction backups, with and without speculative decoding. GSM8K was unchanged.

Unit tests:
- The decode-queue unit tests pass: `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_{unified_memory_move_gate,prefill_complete_integration,deferred_decode_kv_release,decode_queue_cleanup}.py`, `test/registered/unit/managers/test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py`, and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_{decode_radix_lock_ref,decode_retraction_backup,mamba_capacity}.py`.
- Result: 112 passed, the same as on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The only added work is one field read per queued transfer in `pop_transferred`, plus a non-blocking event query for the few requests preallocated in the last iteration. A destination's send waits at most one decode step.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Follow-ups in this revision

Two fixes found in review of the first revision:

- `CommonKVReceiver.__init__` creates `chunk_staging_infos = []`, so a staging `release_room` works for a request that failed or was aborted before its held `send_metadata` ran. Before, the list was created by `send_metadata`, and cleanup of such a request raised and leaked the decode pool pages it had reserved.
- The held send moves from the top of `DecodeTransferQueue.pop_transferred` to after the poll and queue filtering, so only requests still in the transfer queue send their destination. A request that failed or was aborted while its destination was held never tells prefill where to write, and `_defer_release` awaits no drain acknowledgement for it.

New unit tests: `test_receiver_connection_pool.py::TestCommonReceiverLifecycle.test_staging_release_before_send_metadata` and `test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py::TestFailedTransfersDeferOnEveryFailure.test_held_destination_is_sent_only_by_queued_requests`.


</details>

Rebased onto current main to resolve the conflict with #45328. #45328 now defers the decode destination publish under overlap scheduling, which closes this race on the default path, so this PR is re-scoped to the configurations where the destination is still published inline (PP, the staging buffer, HiSparse, or no write-after-read barrier), plus the receiver creating `chunk_staging_infos` up front. A request that fails while its destination is held is now released at once, like one whose deferred publish has not run. The description is updated to match.

cd test/ && python3 registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_pp.py TestDisaggregationDecodePPAccuracy.test_gsm8k

         self._num_published_destinations += 1

+        ready = []

+class TestHeldDestinationPublication(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        _run_as_single_rank(self)
+        reset_context()

+        publish(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy"), role="tokenizer")
+
+    def make_queue(self):
+        queue = DecodeTransferQueue.__new__(DecodeTransferQueue)
+        queue.gloo_group = object()
+        receiver = SimpleNamespace(
+            poll=MagicMock(return_value=KVPoll.WaitingForInput),
+            send_metadata=MagicMock(),
+        )
+        event = SimpleNamespace(query=MagicMock(return_value=True))
+        entry = SimpleNamespace(
+            kv_receiver=receiver,
+            pending_metadata=(event, ("pages", 3, None), {}),
+            is_rebootstrap=False,
+        )
+        queue.queue = [entry]

+    def test_waits_for_every_rank_and_sends_once(self):

+            patch("torch.distributed.get_world_size", return_value=2),
+            patch("torch.distributed.all_reduce") as reduce,

+            # This rank finished its forward; another rank is still writing.

> Hi @libertyeagle, this PR is still a draft, so upstream CI is blocked for it. Will you keep driving it, update it to your latest revision and mark it ready for review? If you'd prefer that we take it over, just say so. Thanks!

@metamergebot  please take over it

Hi @libertyeagle, thanks for handing this over. The branch now carries the follow-ups found in review (the receiver creates `chunk_staging_infos` before `send_metadata` is held, and the held destination is sent only for requests still in the transfer queue, with no drain acknowledgement awaited for one that never sent it), rebased onto current main after #47063. The bot cannot take a PR out of draft, so two small asks:

1. Please mark this PR **Ready for review** so CI can run (pr-gate blocks all tests on a draft).
2. Please replace the PR description with the updated one below: it documents the follow-ups and fixes the "before it polls" sentence.

<details>
<summary>Updated PR description</summary>

## Motivation

On a PD decode server with overlap scheduling, a request that finished at step k−1 is still a row of forward k, because forward k was launched before the scheduler processed step k−1's results. `process_batch_result` frees that request's KV pages while forward k is still in flight. On the next iteration, `process_decode_queue` can preallocate those pages for a new request, and `DecodePreallocQueue._send_kv_metadata` sends them to prefill right away.

The prefill then writes the pages by RDMA, and no CUDA stream orders that write. If the RDMA lands before forward k writes the finished row's KV, forward k overwrites part of the new request's transferred KV. The new request then decodes from wrong KV, and nothing reports an error.

Two other paths already guard against this by waiting for the forward stream before they reuse pages:
- prebuilt requests (`get_new_prebuilt_batch`);
- retraction restore and write-through (#42701, #42702).

The prealloc → transfer path is the one that remains, and `wait_stream` cannot order a remote RDMA write.

Each hit corrupts one position per finished row with plain decode. With speculative decoding it corrupts one verify window, and that window can fall on a page beyond the request's committed length. Hits need a nearly full decode pool, so that a freed page is reused at once, and a prefill that is already waiting for decode memory, so that its RDMA lands within one forward.

## Modifications

When overlap scheduling is on and the destination is on the device:
- `DecodePreallocQueue._send_kv_metadata` records an event on the forward stream after allocating, instead of calling `send_metadata` right away. The event covers every forward enqueued so far. The `send_metadata` arguments are kept on the request in a new field, `DecodeRequest.pending_metadata`.
- `DecodeTransferQueue.pop_transferred` sends the held metadata once its event completes, after it polls and filters the queue, so only requests still queued send it.
- Nothing blocks. A request dropped from the transfer queue drops its held metadata with it.

The send is delayed by at most the forward in flight, about one decode step, and only while that forward is still running. Host destinations are unchanged, because the H2D copy that follows already waits for the forward.

Every transfer backend gets the fix, since they all receive destinations through `_send_kv_metadata`. That includes the staging path, whose scatter runs on its own stream.

The unit test stand-ins for `DecodeRequest` and the scheduler get the new fields (`pending_metadata=None`, `enable_overlap=False`).

## Accuracy Tests

The corruption is silent, so it was found with a KV integrity checker. The checker seals each transferred page with a checksum on prefill and verifies it when decode accepts the transfer.

The setup was PD 1P1D with overlap scheduling and a decode pool small enough to force retractions, with 4096-token prompts and 2048-token outputs at concurrency 32.

Before this change, with and without speculative decoding:
- Transferred pages failed their checksum at accept, while the page identity in the tag still matched.
- Debug output showed the forward for requests that had just finished writing into those pages after the transfer landed.

After this change: no mismatches over repeated runs (8–10 retractions and about 475 accepted transfers each), with `cpu_tensor` and `host_pool` retraction backups, with and without speculative decoding. GSM8K was unchanged.

Unit tests:
- The decode-queue unit tests pass: `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_{unified_memory_move_gate,prefill_complete_integration,deferred_decode_kv_release,decode_queue_cleanup}.py`, `test/registered/unit/managers/test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py`, and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_{decode_radix_lock_ref,decode_retraction_backup,mamba_capacity}.py`.
- Result: 112 passed, the same as on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The only added work is one field read per queued transfer in `pop_transferred`, plus a non-blocking event query for the few requests preallocated in the last iteration. A destination's send waits at most one decode step.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Follow-ups in this revision

Two fixes found in review of the first revision:

- `CommonKVReceiver.__init__` creates `chunk_staging_infos = []`, so a staging `release_room` works for a request that failed or was aborted before its held `send_metadata` ran. Before, the list was created by `send_metadata`, and cleanup of such a request raised and leaked the decode pool pages it had reserved.
- The held send moves from the top of `DecodeTransferQueue.pop_transferred` to after the poll and queue filtering, so only requests still in the transfer queue send their destination. A request that failed or was aborted while its destination was held never tells prefill where to write, and `_defer_release` awaits no drain acknowledgement for it.

New unit tests: `test_receiver_connection_pool.py::TestCommonReceiverLifecycle.test_staging_release_before_send_metadata` and `test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py::TestFailedTransfersDeferOnEveryFailure.test_held_destination_is_sent_only_by_queued_requests`.


</details>

Rebased onto current main to resolve the conflict with #45328. #45328 now defers the decode destination publish under overlap scheduling, which closes this race on the default path, so this PR is re-scoped to the configurations where the destination is still published inline (PP, the staging buffer, HiSparse, or no write-after-read barrier), plus the receiver creating `chunk_staging_infos` up front. A request that fails while its destination is held is now released at once, like one whose deferred publish has not run. The description is updated to match.
